chapter: Bebop, Tadd Dameron, Slam Stewart and Europe
title: Beryl Booker playing an arrangement in B natural
summary: Collins tells how a tipsy Beryl Booker played a rehearsed tune a half step off, perfectly, in B natural.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: She made everything right. She could play anything wrong and make it sound right. She was -- I don't think Beryl read. We would rehearse a tune, very intricate arrangement, this is with Slam Stewart, I'm still with Slam. And so we're going to do it tonight, and Beryl would get juiced. She drank quite a bit. So we probably did this

arrangement during rehearsal in B flat, and so we're going to do this tune tonight, we're going to get to work. And Beryl is juiced and she'd get to where we did it, she'd play the whole thing in B natural, which is the hardest key in the world, and play it note for note, nothing -- you know, nothing changed.
